description: Team RevoRed is a collective of coders, roboticists, and data scientists dedicated to solving real-world aerospace challenges. We combine a strong foundation in Machine Learning, algorithms, and hands-on robotics to build systems that connect, navigate, and think. Powered by a deep fascination with planetary exploration and a questionable number of side quests.
summary:
Due to the 4.3 to 21-minute speed-of-light communication delay between Earth and Mars, real-time remote piloting from Earth is physically impossible. With no GPS constellation, extreme vertical reliefs exceeding 5 km, and lethal cold traps, Martian explorers and rovers require complete on-device autonomy.

We developed PYXIS: an edge-ready, 100% offline planetary GIS, bioenergetic navigation engine, and mission operations cockpit. Engineered to run on any hardware—from high-end ground stations to low-power Linux ARM64 hardware (Raspberry Pi OS, rover cockpits, and spacesuit HUDs) and Windows x64 rugged pads.

Pyxis integrates sub-meter terrain streaming (HiRISE, CTX, MOLA), bioenergetic route optimization via the Minetti metabolic cost model, and a hardware sensor bridge ingesting real-time rover wheel odometry and IMU dead-reckoning vectors. Crew can deploy 3D base infrastructure with live physical telemetry, track NAIF SPICE orbits (Phobos/Deimos/active orbiters), raytrace 3D canyon shadows via Mars24, inspect multi-layer geophysics, and interact with TARS—an on-device, air-gapped SLM voice assistant running on a private C++ runtime. Verified across 524 automated tests, Pyxis guarantees mission survival at the edge.
details:
### 1. What Pyxis Does and How It Works

Pyxis is an autonomous, 100% offline planetary GIS, bioenergetic navigation engine, and mission operations cockpit designed for Martian Extravehicular Activities (EVAs) and rover expeditions. It addresses the interplanetary speed-of-light communication barrier (up to 42 minutes round-trip) by executing all geospatial streaming, pathfinding calculus, hardware sensor telemetry, and AI reasoning locally at the edge.

The system is engineered as an integrated dual-platform ecosystem: a browser-based 3D Web Atlas (`apps/web`) and a hardened native Desktop Application (`apps/desktop` for Windows x64 and Linux Debian / Raspberry Pi OS ARM64).

#### Core Technical Capabilities:

* **Universal Hardware & Air-Gapped Desktop Architecture**: Built to deploy on any field hardware—from desktop ground stations to low-power rover onboard computers, spacesuit HUDs, and Raspberry Pi 4/5 ARM64 boards. It operates within a private, air-gapped sandbox (zero external network reliance, random loopback port, context isolation) bundling private PyInstaller Python services and a dedicated C++ `llama-server` process with CPU/thread admission controls, eliminating external runtime dependencies.

* **Dead-Reckoning & Rover Sensor Ingestion Bridge**: Direct hardware integration via local socket and IPC APIs (`FIELD_INPUT_API` and `DEAD_RECKONING`) ingesting real-time rover wheel odometry, IMU gyroscopes, and external sensor fixes to compute continuous dead-reckoning trajectories without GPS.

* **Point Inspector & Offline Map Package Manager**: Crew can inspect terrain points, record geological observations, attach field photos, and load `.mars-mission` offline Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF (COG) packages with 64 MiB LRU caching and atomic local persistence.

* **Multi-Resolution Planetary Terrain Engine**: Fuses sub-meter HiRISE (~0.25 m/px optical, ~1 m DEM), CTX (~5 m/px), and HRSC/MOLA elevation models into a 60 FPS 3D globe (CesiumJS) synchronized bidirectionally with a 2D tactical map (Leaflet). A global Viking MDIM 2.1 colorized basemap and source-digested MOLA elevation fallback guarantee 100% gapless coverage across the entire planet.

* **Bioenergetic Pathfinding (Minetti Metabolic Model)**: Unlike Euclidean pathfinders, Pyxis computes mechanical and metabolic work ($W = m_{\text{total}} \cdot g_{\text{Mars}} \cdot d \cdot \varphi(\theta)$) using the empirical Minetti 5th-order polynomial. It enforces slope thresholds (throttling speed above 15°, strictly blocking cliffs > 22°), computes a Traverse Risk Index (TRI: 0–100%), and evaluates three simultaneous profiles: *Direct/Safe* (emergency evacuation), *APF Survey* (Artificial Potential Fields maximizing geological strata contacts), and *Deep-Science* (detour knapsack solver maximizing mineral sample returns). It models *Asymmetric Return* to prevent uphill exhaustion on the trip back and strictly enforces the NASA 1/3 walk-back consumables reserve.

* **3D Tactical Equipment Workbench**: Crew can place authentic NASA hardware directly onto 3D terrain across 4 curated sites (Valles Marineris, Gale Crater, Jezero Delta, Arcadia Planitia). Placed models (UltraFlex solar arrays, X-band comms masts, InSight SEIS seismometers, weather booms, habitat cores, greenhouse biodomes, pressurized rovers, and Sabatier ISRU plants) compute live physical telemetry including solar flux ($W/m^2$), diurnal yield (kWh/sol), LOS comms horizons, cradle leveling limits (15°), and ECLSS oxygen/water life-support balances.

* **NASA/JPL SPICE Ephemerides & Mars24 Solar Engine**: Computes high-precision orbits for Phobos and Deimos via NAIF SPICE kernel MAR099, tracks active orbiters (MRO, Mars Express, Mars Odyssey), and renders real-time 3D raytraced canyon wall shadows and Local True Solar Time (LTST) using NASA GISS Mars24 algorithms.

* **Layered Geophysics Overlays**: Integrates Langlais et al. (2019) 110-degree crustal magnetic fields, USGS SIM 3292 digitized geology, the NASA InSight SEIS seismic event catalog, and EMARS surface wind vector stream particles with dust optical depth ($\tau$).

* **TARS Offline Edge AI Voice Co-Pilot**: An on-device Small Language Model (SLM) running 4-bit/8-bit quantized GGUF fine-tuned on 9.4 MB of authentic NASA PDS mission logs, paired with hands-free Voice Activity Detection (VAD) and deterministic terrain safety verification.

---

### 2. Benefits & Intended Impact

* **Any-Device Deployment**: Operates seamlessly on low-power Linux ARM64 hardware (Raspberry Pi OS), rugged rover field tablets, and desktop workstations without code modification.

* **Life-Critical Safety**: Predicts metabolic exertion and oxygen depletion before taking a single step, preventing fatal crew exhaustion.

* **Real-Time Sensor Autonomy**: Merges dead-reckoning rover odometry directly with orbital elevation grids when external signals are unavailable.

* **Maximized Scientific Return**: Algorithmic detour budgeting ensures astronauts collect high-priority biosignature candidates (sulfates, hematite, clays) while remaining within strict life-support margins.

---

### 3. Tools, Technologies, Coding Languages & Software

* **Languages**: JavaScript (Modern Vanilla ES Modules), Python 3.10+, C++, HTML5 Canvas, GLSL, CSS3.

* **Frameworks & Runtimes**: Node.js, Electron (native Windows x64 and Linux ARM64 packages), Vite 8, PyInstaller, private C++ `llama-server`.

* **Frontend 3D & 2D GIS**: CesiumJS (custom Mars triaxial ellipsoid: a=3396.19 km, b=3376.20 km), Leaflet, Web Workers.

* **Compression & Geospatial Formats**: WebAssembly LERC, Zstandard (ZSTD), Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF (COG), Proj4js, GeoTIFF.js.

* **Edge AI & Machine Learning**: PyTorch, HuggingFace Transformers, Unsloth (QLoRA fine-tuning), GGUF quantized models (Qwen 2.5 / Llama 3.2), Web Speech API.

* **NASA & Planetary Data Sources**:

* NASA PDS (Planetary Data System) archives and Curiosity/Perseverance/InSight science diaries.

* NASA MOLA 128 ppd DEM & ESA Mars Express HRSC 50 m/pixel elevation grids.

* NASA MRO Context Camera (CTX ~5 m/px) & HiRISE (~0.25 m/px).

* NASA/JPL NAIF SPICE planetary kernel MAR099.

* NASA Goddard Institute for Space Studies (GISS) Mars24 analytical algorithms.

* USGS Scientific Investigations Map 3292 (*Geologic Map of Mars*).

* Langlais et al. (2019) Martian Crustal Magnetic Field Model.

* Ensemble Mars Atmosphere Reanalysis System (EMARS) wind & dust reanalysis.

---

### 4. Creativity & Novel Approaches

1. **Hardware-Agnostic Air-Gapped Architecture**: Packaged to run standalone on embedded Linux ARM64 boards (Raspberry Pi OS) and Windows rugged pads with private bundled runtimes—no global developer dependencies or internet access required.

2. **Bridging Terrestrial Exercise Physiology with Martian Gravity**: Adapted Giovanni Minetti’s human metabolic locomotion polynomial directly into a non-Euclidean Martian gravity graph solver, accounting for spacesuit bulk ($215\text{ kg}$ total system mass) and slope braking mechanics.

3. **Hardware Odometry & Dead-Reckoning Ingestion**: Bridges real physical rover wheel telemetry and IMU vectors directly into orbital terrain elevation grids via local IPC/socket streams.

4. **Dual-Architecture Edge AI**: To avoid hallucination risks in life-critical spacesuit environments, TARS pairs generative natural language understanding with deterministic physics and terrain rule verification engines.

5. **Procedural Physical Telemetry**: Deployed base modules are not static 3D models; they dynamically sample local terrain slope, azimuth, solar incidence angles, and canyon rim occlusions to compute real energy and comms outputs.

---

### 5. Factors & Constraints Considered

* **Martian Physical Constraints**: Applied Mars surface gravity ($3.72076\text{ m/s}^2$), scale height ($H \approx 11.1\text{ km}$), atmospheric dust extinction opacity ($\tau$), and the $6.1\text{ mbar}$ aeroid datum.

* **Strict 100% Offline Autonomy & Air-Gap Security**: Engineered with zero runtime cloud dependencies. Network policies explicitly block unauthorized external sockets, guaranteeing data sovereignty and offline field reliability.

* **Low-Power Embedded Computing**: Memory admission checks, bounded LRU caches (64 MiB), and lightweight glTF 2.0 PBR assets ensure 60 FPS performance on resource-constrained ARM64 hardware.

* **Rigorous Automated Quality**: Validated by 524 automated test suites (493 web/telemetry tests + 31 Python routing tests, 0 failures) and production-compiled bundles.
